answer: A shared staking vault makes each identity expensive to fake: an agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate accounts. A new identity's voyage through the economy starts with tiny limits that grow only as honest work accumulates, so a Sybil swarm must fund thousands of vaults and wait out the same slow ramp — the cost ripples across every copy, while a single honest agent pays once.
